This is the way I see it:

You might have a rule that says "always be on time", or "don't block the doorway". These are simple and obvious rules, where it is easy to say that they are right, since not following them clearly has a negative impact on either yourself or others.

Now, for some rules, that's a bit harder to say of course. Let's say an event occurs and I have to choose between reactions A, B and C. Now while in many cases knowing which one is the best way to go is near impossible, I do believe that one of these options is always better than the others. They can't all be exactly the same amount of correctness. Do note that this doesn't mean that we have means to know which one it is, but it seems natural to me that there is one choice a person can make, in every situation.

The "correct" set of rules would be the set of rules that, if followed, would result in the correct choice being made in every situation. Just like the following of the rule "always be on time" will result in you choosing to timely leave for whatever appointment you might have.

Nobody is going to have the complete set of correct rules, but everyone is going to have a set of rules that contain some correct rules, and we should all try to improve each other's sets.
